_comment: Declarative machine state. The dotfiles-setup skill reads this file and applies it. Paths use %VAR% placeholders that are expanded at deploy time, so nothing here is pinned to one username. JSON rather than YAML because the installer runs on node: builtins with zero dependencies.
_softwareComment: This list is the ONLY place a package id is allowed to live. The installer prints its install hints from these ids rather than from string literals in code, because the one id that was written in code (a wrong tree-sitter id) went unchecked for exactly as long as it had nowhere to be compared against. Every id here is verified with `winget show --id <id> --exact`. Detection order is detectOnPath, then detectPath, then winget: the first two exist because software installed through another channel is still installed, and winget reports only what winget put there.

software.name: Tabby
software.why: The terminal the whole dotfiles profile targets.

software.name: Neovim
software.why: Editor config in nvim/ expects 0.10 or later.

software.name: Git
software.why: Ships git-bash, which is the default Tabby profile (local:git-bash), and is what clones this repo in the first place.

software.name: Node.js
software.why: Runs install.mjs, so it is the one thing that has to exist before any of this applies. Usually installed from the nodejs.org MSI or a version manager, none of which winget can see, which is why detection is PATH-first.

software.name: GitHub CLI
software.why: Repo and PR work from the terminal.

software.name: ripgrep
software.why: Backs telescope live grep. The binary is rg, not ripgrep.

software.name: tree-sitter CLI
software.why: nvim-treesitter tracks its main branch, which builds parsers through this CLI instead of shipping them, so a fresh editor needs it plus a C compiler. 0.26 or later. Commonly installed with `npm i -g tree-sitter-cli`, which winget cannot see.

software.name: Proton Drive
software.why: The only cloud sync on this machine; backs up Pictures.

software.name: Proton Authenticator
software.why: 2FA, same vendor as the rest of the Proton stack.

software.name: Logitech G HUB
software.why: Mouse and keyboard profiles; onboard profiles persist without it running.

software.name: G-Helper
software.why: ASUS fan and performance control. Runs as a portable exe dropped in the Startup folder rather than a winget install, so winget correctly reports it absent; detectPath is what actually answers whether it is there.

startup._comment: scope 'user' is HKCU Run and applies with no elevation. scope 'machine' is HKLM Run and is recorded for reference only, never written by the installer. scope 'startup-folder' is a file the user drops in themselves.

enabled.name: Tabby
enabled.why: Boots straight to the tray. --hidden is Tabby's own documented flag ('Start minimized'); the boot path then calls Electron's focus() rather than show(), so a hidden window stays hidden. Ctrl-Space drops it down.

enabled.name: Proton Drive
enabled.why: Tray-resident sync, no window at login.

enabled.name: Proton VPN
enabled.why: Launcher hands off to the packaged app's StartupTask. Written verbatim via 'command' because Proton registers it with the exe UNQUOTED and the argument QUOTED, and that argument contains & and ?, so re-composing it in the usual "exe" arg shape would change how it parses. The %20 is URL encoding, not an environment variable, so the expander must leave it alone.

enabled.name: Discord
enabled.why: Tray only. Discord's updater shim is the real startup target, not Discord.exe.

enabled.name: LGHUB
enabled.why: Tray only. Peripherals keep working without it; it is only needed to change DPI, lighting or macros.

enabled.name: AMDNoiseSuppression
enabled.why: AMD microphone noise removal. The one entry with no minimize flag; kept because it is a driver-level feature, but it is the weakest-value item on this list.

enabled.name: GHelper
enabled.why: ASUS fan and performance control, native tray app. Lives as a portable exe in the Startup folder rather than a Run entry.

enabled.name: SecurityHealth
enabled.why: Windows Security tray icon. Windows owns this entry; recorded so the list is complete, never written by the installer.

disabled.why: Design-tool font helper; only needed while Figma is open.
uTorrent Web tray; torrent work happens in torlink.
Game launcher has no reason to boot with the OS.
Edge preloading itself at login. Suffix is a per-machine hex id, so this must match by prefix.
Copilot preloading itself at login. Same per-machine hex suffix.
AMD User Experience Program launcher, the telemetry front end. See privacy.services for the service half.
Heavy vendor updater; launch Creative Cloud on demand instead.
Creative Cloud companion process, same reasoning.
Drawing-tablet driver tray; only needed when the tablet is plugged in.
Java update scheduler, a classic always-on nuisance.

knownFolders._comment: Policy: the user profile folders stay local and are never redirected into a cloud-sync folder. Screenshots deliberately sits OUTSIDE Pictures, because Pictures is what Proton Drive backs up and the screenshot history does not belong in cloud backup.
knownFolders._regNameNote: regName is the value name Windows actually stores under User Shell Folders, which is not the friendly name: Documents is 'Personal' and Pictures is 'My Pictures'. It is read to detect drift before repointing.

shell.name: Pictures
shell.why: Local on disk; Proton Drive backs this folder up.

shell.name: Screenshots
shell.why: Deliberately moved out of Pictures so Win+PrtScn captures are not swept into cloud backup. This is NOT the Windows default, which is %USERPROFILE%\Pictures\Screenshots.

userShellFolderValues.name: {F42EE2D3-909F-4907-8871-4C22FC0BF756}
userShellFolderValues.why: The 'This PC' Documents node. Not covered by SHSetKnownFolderPath, and it silently kept pointing at a deleted OneDrive path until it was fixed by hand.

userShellFolderValues.name: {0DDD015D-B06C-45D5-8C4C-F59713854639}
userShellFolderValues.why: The 'This PC' Pictures node, same failure mode.

privacy._comment: Everything here needs administrator rights, so the installer never applies it directly. It emits a reviewable script instead (--privacy).

services.name: DiagTrack
services.why: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry, the main Windows telemetry pipe. Cost: Feedback Hub stops working and some Windows Update diagnostics go quiet. Windows Update, Defender and activation are unaffected.

services.name: AUEPLauncher
services.why: AMD User Experience Program Data Uploader. Pure usage-data collection with no user-facing function.

scheduledTasks.name: Consolidator
scheduledTasks.why: CEIP data collection. No functional loss.

scheduledTasks.name: UsbCeip
scheduledTasks.why: CEIP USB data collection. No functional loss.

deliberatelyNotApplied.name: Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser
deliberatelyNotApplied.why: Sits in the same task folder family but is app-compatibility plumbing feeding upgrade readiness, not telemetry. Left enabled on purpose.

deliberatelyNotApplied.name: AllowTelemetry policy
deliberatelyNotApplied.why: Left at 1 (Required). Windows 11 Home floors telemetry at Required regardless of the policy value, so setting it to 0 would imply an off switch that does not exist. Not worth pretending.

cloudSync._comment: See machine/README.md. OneDrive removal is documented but deliberately never automated, because online-only placeholder files must be hydrated first or the data is destroyed.

syncedFolders.why: Backed up by Proton Drive's folder-backup mapping.

excludedFromSync.why: Screenshot history is high-volume and low-value; kept out of cloud backup by living outside Pictures.
